problems.title: Track signs in a fraction
problems.question: Evaluate 5(9-13)(-4)/[8(9-14)].
problems.idea: Compute each difference first.
formulas: A positive number divided by a negative number is negative.
steps: The numerator is 5·(-4)·(-4)=80.
The denominator is 8·(-5)=-40, so the quotient is -2.

problems.title: Two isosceles triangles around a parallel line
problems.question: In the diagram RT=TN=NE=ET, ET∥MN, and RNU=20°. Find ETR.
problems.idea: The first three equal lengths form an equilateral triangle.
formulas: Equilateral angles are 60°; isosceles base angles are equal.
steps: Triangle ETN is equilateral. Parallelism gives TNU=60°, hence TNR=60°-20°=40°.
In triangle NTR, NT=TR makes both base angles 40°, so NTR=100°.

problems.title: Minimum product of consecutive integers
problems.question: Find the least possible product of six consecutive integers.
problems.idea: A block crossing from negative to positive contains zero.
formulas: Six negative factors give a positive product; a factor zero makes the product zero.
steps: If all six integers have one sign, the product is positive because there are an even number of negative factors.
If both signs occur, zero is one of the consecutive integers, so the product is zero.
For example -2,-1,0,1,2,3 attains zero.

problems.title: Proportional parts of a decimal
problems.question: Split 0.6 in ratio 5/2:5/3:5/6. Find the largest part.
problems.idea: Clear the common denominator.
steps: The ratio has 6 units, each 0.6/6=0.1.
The largest part is 3·0.1=0.3.

problems.title: Congruent triangles share a diagonal
problems.question: Quadrilateral MNPQ has perimeter 28 cm, NQ=9 cm, and the marked angle pairs 1=2,3=4. Find the perimeter of QMN.
problems.idea: The diagonal and matching endpoint angles make the two triangles congruent.
formulas: ASA congruence; equal triangles have equal corresponding side sums.
steps: Triangles NQM,NQP share NQ and have equal adjacent angle pairs as marked.
Thus their outer two-side sums are equal, each 28/2=14.
Adding NQ gives triangle perimeter 14+9=23.

problems.title: Middle of nine consecutive numbers
problems.question: Nine consecutive positive integers have mean 2016. Find the smallest.
problems.idea: The mean is the central fifth term.
steps: There are four terms before the middle.
The smallest is 2016-4=2012.

problems.title: Minimize a sum of distances
problems.question: Find the minimum of |a+1|+|a+2|+…+|a+7|.
problems.idea: The median of the seven target points minimizes their distance sum.
steps: The three pairs contribute at least 6+4+2=12, and |a+4|≥0.
At a=-4 all four lower bounds are attained.

problems.title: Catch-up time
problems.question: A car at 36 km/h follows a cyclist at 30 km/h with a 2 km lead. Find catch-up time.
problems.idea: The gap closes at the speed difference.
steps: The relative speed is 6 km/h.
Time=2/6 hour=20 minutes.

problems.title: Combine like terms before substitution
problems.question: Evaluate -a-5-2a+3 for a=2/3.
problems.idea: Collect the a terms and constants.
steps: The expression is -3a-2.

problems.title: Compare consecutive blocks of four integers
problems.question: How much greater is the sum of the next four consecutive integers than that of the first four?
problems.idea: Each corresponding term rises by 4.
formulas: Total change=number of terms·change per term.
steps: Write the blocks as n,…,n+3 and n+4,…,n+7.
There are four increases of 4, giving 16.

problems.title: Three linked triangle angles
problems.question: One triangle angle is 20° greater than a second and one third of the third. Find the smallest.
problems.idea: Express all angles in terms of the named angle t.
steps: The angles are 40°,20°,120°; the smallest is 20°.

problems.title: Chicken-days of food
problems.question: Eight chickens eat 3 kg in 6 days. How long do three chickens take to eat 24 kg?
problems.idea: Scale the food and number of chickens separately.
steps: Three chickens eat 3/16 kg per day.
The time for 24 kg is 24/(3/16)=128 days.

problems.title: Perpendicular bisector in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: AB=BC with base angles 80°. The perpendicular bisector of AB meets BC at D. Find ADC.
problems.idea: D is equidistant from A and B.
steps: B=20°. In isosceles ADB, ABD=BAD=20°, so ADB=140°.
DC is opposite DB along the same line, so ADC=180°-140°=40°.

problems.title: A right triangle from an angle difference
problems.question: Two triangle angles differ by the third. The median from the largest-angle vertex is 4.2 cm. Find the largest side.
problems.idea: The largest angle must be 90°.
formulas: If A=B+C and A+B+C=180°, then A=90°; median to hypotenuse=half the hypotenuse.
steps: The angle relation makes the triangle right-angled.
The hypotenuse is twice the median, 2·4.2=8.4 cm.
problems.note: None of the printed options 20,22,24,26,28,30 matches. The options appear displaced from another question.

problems.title: Remaining horse-days
problems.question: Hay feeds 10 horses for 15 days. After 2 days, 5 horses leave. For how many more days does the remainder feed the other 5?
problems.idea: Use horse-days, subtracting food already used.
steps: The remaining stock is 150-20=130 horse-days.
For 5 horses it lasts 130/5=26 more days.
problems.note: The printed options do not include 26. Including the first two days would give 28 total days, but the question asks how long the remaining stock lasts.

problems.title: Find a base from its relation to a leg
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base b=2s/3+1 dm and perimeter 3.4 dm. Find b.
problems.idea: Use two equal legs s.

problems.title: The printed equation contradicts itself
problems.question: Solve the equation as printed: x:0.5+3=x:0.5-3, where colon means division.
problems.idea: Both x terms are identical.
steps: The printed equation is 2x+3=2x-3.
Subtract 2x to get 3=-3, which is impossible.
problems.note: The source PDF has a division colon on both sides. If the first colon were intended as multiplication, 0.5x+3=2x-3 would instead give x=4; that is a correction, not a solution to the printed equation.

problems.title: Distribute and combine before evaluating
problems.question: Evaluate -6(2a/3-b/6)+4(0.75a-b/12) for a=-1,b=3/2.
problems.idea: Simplify the whole expression first.
steps: The expression becomes -4a+b+3a-b/3=-a+2b/3.
At the given values it is 1+1=2.

problems.title: A boy does not count himself as a classmate
problems.question: Dito has 7 more boy classmates than girl classmates. The class has twice as many boys as girls. How many girl classmates does Ana have?
problems.idea: Count Dito and Ana correctly.
formulas: If totals are B,G, then B-1=G+7 and B=2G.
steps: Thus 2G-1=G+7, giving G=8.
Ana is one of those girls, so she has 8-1=7 girl classmates.

problems.title: Planned profit before a discount
problems.question: A shop sells a book 10% below its planned price and still makes 8% profit. What profit had it planned?
problems.idea: Work backward from actual selling price.
steps: If cost is C, the actual price is 1.08C.
The planned price was 1.08C/0.9=1.2C.
Thus the planned profit was 20%.
problems.answer: 20%; none of the listed numerical choices.

problems.title: An orthocentre angle depends on the branch
problems.question: The lines of altitudes to BC and AB meet at M. Given BAC=25°, find ABM.
problems.idea: M is the orthocentre, so BM is also an altitude.
formulas: BM⊥AC; an angle with a perpendicular is 90°±the original angle.
steps: Since BA makes 25° with AC, the line BM makes an acute angle 65° with BA.
The angle between the rays BA and BM is 65° when M lies toward the foot of the B-altitude, or 115° when M lies on the opposite ray.
For an acute triangle as sketched it is 65°. An obtuse angle at B can give 115°.
problems.answer: 65° for the acute configuration shown; 115° is possible for an obtuse configuration.
problems.note: The listed options include only 115°. The wording does not specify the obtuse configuration needed to select that answer, and the sketch is not marked obtuse.

problems.title: An equilateral triangle inside a 120-degree apex
problems.question: AB=BC and B=120°. E,F lie on AC with AE=EB and FC=FB=2.1. Find the perimeter of EBF.
problems.idea: Split the apex angle using two small isosceles triangles.
formulas: Base angles A=C=30°; equal sides give equal opposite angles.
steps: AE=EB makes ABE=30°. FC=FB makes FBC=30°.
Thus EBF=120°-30°-30°=60°. Also EB=FB=2.1 by symmetry of the two end configurations.
Triangle EBF is equilateral, so its perimeter is 3·2.1=6.3.

problems.title: Average ages with group weights
problems.question: Thirty women average 30 years; twenty men average 40. Find the average of all fifty teachers.
problems.idea: Use total ages, not the unweighted mean of group means.
steps: Total age=900+800=1700 years.
Divide by 50 to get 34 years.

problems.title: A 36–72–72 triangle and its bisectors
problems.question: In isosceles ABC with B=36°, the A,C bisectors meet at O. D is the foot of the A-bisector on BC. If CO=m,OD=n, find the perimeter.
problems.idea: Use the angles to relate the short base and equal sides.
formulas: Golden ratio φ=(1+√5)/2, φ²=φ+1; in a 36–72–72 triangle equal side/base=φ.
steps: Symmetry gives AO=CO=m. Triangle ACD has angles 36°,72°,72°, so AC=AD=m+n.
Triangle COD has C=36°,D=72°,O=72°, so CD=CO=m. The base ratio gives AC=φm; hence n=(φ-1)m.
Each equal side is φAC=φ²m=(2m+n).
Perimeter=AC+2AB=(m+n)+2(2m+n)=5m+3n.

problems.title: Exterior bisectors meet at an excentre
problems.question: The pictured exterior-angle bisectors at B,C meet at a 66° angle. Find A.
problems.idea: The angle in their intersection triangle is half the sum of B,C.
steps: The two exterior half-angles at B,C are (180°-B)/2,(180°-C)/2.
Their remaining triangle angle is (B+C)/2=90°-A/2.
Set 66°=90°-A/2 to get A=48°.
